name: Glory
desc: The half of the sky nobody looks at — everything here is built around the antisolar point, where your own shadow falls: a tight nest of glory rings backscattered out of the fog, a broad ghostly fogbow with supernumerary arcs ringing inside its edge, a reversed secondary with Alexander's dark band held between them, and a retroreflected heiligenschein burning at the centre. One knob does it all: shrink the droplets and the colours smear into a white fogbow with a wide glory, grow them and it sharpens into a true rainbow. Purely additive, so it lies over a scene as light.

energy.doc: brightness of the whole display (master knob)

scale.doc: angular scale of the sky — sets how big the 41-degree bow is on the frame

drop.doc: droplet radius, the one physical knob: small drops smear the bow into a white fogbow and blow the glory rings wide (~9 deg), large drops sharpen it into a true rainbow with tight supernumeraries and pull the glory in (~3 deg)

density.doc: fog thickness — the luminous mist, the heiligenschein and the strength of the secondary bow

speed.doc: fog drift and antisolar-point wander rate

hue.doc: colour cast over the true dispersion (205 = neutral; the spectral order red-outside on the primary is preserved)

x.doc: antisolar point x — where the observer's shadow falls

y.doc: antisolar point y (opposite the sun, so low sun = high antisolar point)

bows.doc: which of the display is showing: everything, the glory rings alone, the primary bow alone, or primary plus secondary with Alexander's dark band between

style.doc: aesthetic: cool mist, saturated colour, a desaturated Brocken haunting, a dispersion-free silver display, or a dim blue moonbow

seed.doc: seed — fog patch layout, drift phases

alpha.doc: layer opacity — defaults below full so it sits politely over a live scene
